title: Interview snippets and action items - Rafaela Mendez
content:
Quick scratchpad from today's loop with Sahil Kaur. This is informal — raw impressions, verbatim snippets I scribbled, and concrete action items for follow-up. Use when writing the panel debrief.

High-level gut: strong systems person with good latency/cost intuition for serving. Comfortable with GPU concepts at a high level (batching, memory tradeoffs, KV cache), less confident on lower-level kernel/compilation internals. Good communicator; frames tradeoffs well. Could be a solid hire for runtime team if we want someone who can move features into production quickly and partner with infra.

What went well (notes + quotes):
- System design question (scalable chat-serving architecture): Sahil sketched a multi-tier router -> stateless API -> GPU pool model and emphasized smart routing by SLOs and model variants. Quote: "Prefer soft-fallbacks so customers don't experience 500s — route to cheaper variant if latency target slipping". Clear product-minded thinking.
- Latency troubleshooting (given a noisy tail scenario): suggested end-to-end tracing, prefix caching, and prioritized request queues. Suggested using token-level sampling to identify long sequences as an immediate signal. Practical steps that match our production toolkit.
- Practical coding / pseudo: wrote a compact LRU-based KV cache eviction approach and explained how staleness windows interact with batching. Sketch was high value and would translate into a 1-2 week spike to prototype.

Weak spots / red flags:
- When pressed on quantization numeric stability (FP16 vs INT8 tradeoffs), he had surface-level knowledge but couldn't explain calibration procedures or dequantization edge cases. Might need pairing with someone from applied-ml for deeper model-on-hardware decisions.
- Not much hands-on with custom CUDA kernels or TVM-like compilation pipelines — more familiar with PyTorch/XLA and vendor runtimes. If we need a kernel hacker, probably not the right hire.

Behavioral / org fit notes:
- Comfortable with ambiguous requirements; repeatedly referenced cost/latency metrics when prioritizing features.
- Emphasized collaboration with product and SRE — asked good questions about our rollout tooling and observability primitives.

Interview vignettes (verbatim lines I captured):
- "I prefer to design routing policies that minimize user-visible fallback. Drop to cheaper variant only when confidence falls below threshold."
- "When you see token timeouts, first check queueing and batching windows — often the default batching policy is the cause."
- On ownership: "I like owning the signal path end-to-end, from request admission to response metrics."

Scoring (personal, rough 1-5):
- System design & architecture: 4
- Production debugging & observability: 4
- Low-level kernels / compiler internals: 2
- ML numeric stability / quantization depth: 2.5
- Communication & cross-team collaboration: 4.5

Overall recommendation (working draft): Strong hire for a feature-focused senior engineer on runtime / serving where we need fast delivery, solid SLO-first thinking, and reliability improvements. Recommend move to final on-site loop (or second round) with emphasis on: 1) a short pairing task on quantization/stability with someone from applied-ml, and 2) a deeper probing question set on resource-constrained batching / memory pressure scenarios.

Concrete action items (for hiring packet / next steps):
- Diego: can you own a 30-min pairing session focused on quantization edge cases? Tentative: next Tue 10/29.
- Nora: please pull log snippets from the last month of our token-timeout incidents and share two concrete examples; Sahil can comment on mitigations during pairing.
- Rafaela (me): write up a short task prompt (<= 2 hours) that exercises design + a small coding component (KV cache & eviction under memory pressure). Attach to the candidate card.
- Recruiter: signal to candidate we want a quick follow-up pairing and ask for top 2 schedule slots in next 10 days.

Open questions I want the loop to answer:
- Can Sahil articulate a concrete calibration flow for quantization tuning (calibration dataset selection, per-channel vs per-tensor, min/max clipping strategies)?
- What is his approach to model sharding across GPUs for very long sequences (KV cache handling + cross-GPU bandwidth concerns)?
- Real-world example of a time he significantly reduced serving unit cost — numbers appreciated.

Notes on scorecard drafting: emphasize production impact metrics (latency, p95, cost delta) and collaboration stories. Avoid framing too much on CUDA/kernel work — that is not mission-critical for this hire.

Misc: candidate curious about our Dedicated offering and private deployment constraints (KMS/HSM). Asked about ramp plan for new hires owning customer incidents. Good sign.

End of scratchpad. Will refine into a panel-ready debrief after Diego pairing and Nora's artifact pull.
hire_recommendation: proceed-to-pairing-with-applied-ml (strong hire if pairing shows quantization competence)
